results.subject: How the elements repo's drag (createDrag / useDrag, plus createDrop, _drag.scss, the guides, tests and showcase pages) works, read-only, as reference material for improving the veneer sortable. Covered: input model, state machine and thresholds, cross-container transfer, placeholders and indicators, auto-scroll, constraints, events and payloads, accessibility writes, shipped styles and tokens, teardown, what the tests pin, and gaps against W3C/APG.

facts.fact: createDrag uses only the HTML5 Drag and Drop API. It listens for dragstart, dragend, dragenter, dragover, dragleave and drop on the host, plus click and mousedown on the host. On the document it listens for keydown, mouseup (capture) and pointerdown (capture). There are no pointermove or touch listeners and no pointer capture.

The PointerEvent objects placed in event details are made up. start, over and drop get new PointerEvent('pointerdown'/'pointermove'/'pointerup') with no coordinates. The tap event gets a PointerEvent built from the click with pointerType hard-coded to 'mouse'. The end event's pointer is always null.

The only keyboard handling is Escape, caught on the document while dragging, which calls resetState(true, true). There is no keyboard way to pick up, move or drop an item, and no arrow-key selection. select() accepts a KeyboardEvent, but no key handler ever calls it.

Inference: browsers usually handle Escape themselves during a native drag (it ends with dragend), so the document keydown listener may never run mid-drag. Also, HTML5 drag-and-drop gives little or no support for touch on many mobile browsers. Neither point is stated in the inputs.

The elements repo positions this as the platform drag-and-drop wrapper. It points continuous manipulation (splitters, sliders) to a separate usePointer, which owns pointerdown, pointermove and pointerup with a body cursor lock.

The reactive state is dragging (boolean), indices (the set being dragged), selected (the click selection), target (the row index under the pointer) and position ('before', 'after', 'into' or null). It lives in an effectScope and is exposed read-only.

The drag lifecycle: dragstart → begin() sets dragging, computes indices, writes dataTransfer, sets the drag image and emits start. dragover → update() sets target and position and emits over. drop → drop() emits drop, reorders if the row belongs to this host, clears the selection and calls resetState(true, false). dragend → resetState(true, true). resetState only emits end if dragging was true, so a drop followed by dragend emits end once, with cancelled:false.
Drag set rule: resolve.indices(start) wins if supplied. Otherwise, if the start row is selected, the whole selection is dragged. Otherwise only the start row is.

Selection: a plain click replaces the selection and sets the anchor. Ctrl/Meta+click toggles a row and moves the anchor. Shift+click selects the range from the anchor. Each change clears the window text selection and emits a select event with { added, removed, anchor, selection }. A pointerdown outside the host clears the selection without emitting any event.

There is no movement threshold and no long-press delay; drag start is left to the platform's dragstart. The drop zone is split at the row midpoint (clientY on the vertical axis, clientX on horizontal) into 'before' or 'after'. 'into' only comes from a custom resolve.zone callback, and that callback can return null to reject a row.
syncRows rewrites every row's classes and draggable flag. queueSync runs it immediately and again in a microtask, so rows that Vue re-renders get fixed up.

reorder() runs only when a list is given, the drag set is not empty, and the position is not 'into'. It removes the sorted indices in reverse order, adjusts the insert point for removed rows that sat above it, splices the items back in, clears the selection, and emits reorder with { from: sorted indices, to: insertion index after removal, items }.
createDrag only reorders when the drop row's parentElement is its own host. Rows are found with extractRow, which only accepts direct [data-index] children of the root.

Moving items between containers is done through createDrop/useDrop. The drop handler reads the source's indices ref (filled only while that source is dragging) to work out what was dropped; the drag carries no custom data. The page's own source/target example uses items (read-only) plus target:false on the tray.

createDrop tracks an over ref, using relatedTarget so nested children don't make it flicker. accept filters on dataTransfer.types, and an empty types list is accepted. It writes effectAllowed and dropEffect, calls on.dragenter/dragover/dragleave/drop, and emits elements:drop:enter, leave and drop with { originalEvent }.
dataTransfer gets setData('text/plain', startIndex) only when list or items is given. The types option is never written to dataTransfer; it is only copied into the over and drop details.

Inference: when items are dropped onto another createDrag host, that host's own indices are empty, so it emits drop but does not splice anything. The source's dragend then reports cancelled:true, because dragend never looks at dropEffect.

There is no placeholder or gap element. The drag image is the row itself, via setDragImage with the grab offset. Feedback is entirely through row classes: dragging, selected (only when not also dragging), drop-target, drop-indicator (hovered and not 'into'), drop-indicator-before and drop-indicator-after.
createDrag has no auto-scroll code (no scroll listeners, rAF loop or edge zones). Inference: any auto-scroll during a drag comes from the browser's native drag-and-drop behaviour.

facts.fact: Axis: 'vertical' (default) or 'horizontal', used only to choose before/after. Nothing locks movement to the axis.

Handles: if a row contains .drag-handle, the row gets draggable=false and each handle gets draggable=true. canStartFrom rejects drags that start under .no-drag, and when a handle exists it requires the drag to start inside it. The mousedown target is remembered (pressedRow/pressedAllowed) because dragstart's target is the draggable element, not the element the user pressed.
There is no disabled-item support: the factory never reads aria-disabled, disabled or a data flag. The showcase writes aria-disabled on tray items, but the factory ignores it.

There are no named groups or shared-list groups. Source/target roles are booleans: isSource = source ?? (auto || effect.allowed || list/items); isTarget = target ?? (effect.drop || list/items). select:false turns off click selection, but tap still fires.

DRAG_EVENTS: tap, start, over, drop, end, reorder, select and clear, named 'elements:drag:{verb}'. They are registered in the public events tree as events.drag, with DROP_EVENTS as events.drop. All are emitted as bubbling, non-cancelable CustomEvents.

Payloads. tap: { index, pointer }. start: { indices, pointer }. over: { index, position, target, pointer, types }. drop: { index|null, position|null, target|null, pointer, types }. end: { cancelled, pointer|null }. reorder: { from, to, items }. select: { added, removed, anchor, selection }. clear: no detail. over and drop are emitted on the row; everything else on the host. Strict runtime guards exist for the tap, start, over and drop details.
None of the events can be cancelled, so a listener cannot veto a drop or a reorder. emit always passes cancelable:false.

createDrag writes no ARIA at all: no role, aria-selected, aria-grabbed, aria-dropeffect, aria-describedby or tabindex, and no live region or announcements. It does not move or restore focus. The only DOM writes are classes and the draggable property.
The showcase writes aria-selected on rows itself, from the selected ref. Its handle is a span with aria-label and title but no role or tabindex.

_drag.scss is in @layer composables. It gives [draggable='true'] cursor:grab, and grabbing on :active or .dragging. .dragging gets opacity 0.5. [data-index].drop-target gets a 12% oklab mix of --color-primary. Before/after indicators are a 2px --color-primary bar drawn with ::before/::after on a row made position:relative, using logical insets.

The styles take values straight from global tokens (--color-primary) or literals (2px, 12%, 0.5). No --set-drag-* tokens exist anywhere in src, and COMPOSABLE_CONTRACTS.drag requires no tokens. The style partial does not loop over variants with palette-each and has no forced-colors, focus-visible or 'into' styles. The .selected and plain .drop-indicator classes get no style there.

The showcase restyles rows in a scoped block with hard-coded values: .selected uses 12% primary with an inset ring, .dragging opacity 0.4, and an indicator inset 0.5rem / -2px with a border radius. Its transitions are hand-written with no reduced-motion guard.

facts.fact: destroy() can be called more than once. The first call removes the on.* listeners, all host and document listeners, and stops the effect scope. Every call then strips all DRAG_ROW_CLASSES, sets draggable=false on rows and handles when auto is on, and clears the selection. useDrag creates the factory in a post-flush watch on the element ref and destroys it on cleanup or when the ref changes.

The page tells consumers to use useDrop accept ['text/plain'] for drags from useDrag, but createDrag only sets text/plain when list or items is given.

The elements drag is a thin HTML5 drag-and-drop wrapper keyed on rows that are direct [data-index] children. Its strengths: a selection model with an anchor (click, Ctrl, Shift) and multi-row drags; midpoint before/after hit-testing with a pluggable zone/indices resolver; list splicing that corrects the insert index; handle and .no-drag gating that remembers the mousedown target; state shown as classes; and named 'elements:drag:*' CustomEvents plus a separate drop-zone factory. It has no pointer or touch path, no keyboard move, no ARIA or live announcements, no focus handling, no auto-scroll, no placeholder, no disabled items or groups, no cancelable events, no tokenized styles, and its tests cover selection only.

gaps.gap: There is no way to reorder without dragging: no keyboard pick-up/move/drop and no single-pointer alternative such as move up/down. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 (Dragging Movements) and the APG listbox 'rearrangeable options' guidance call for one. This is outside knowledge; the elements guides contain no APG drag material.

gaps.gap: There are no screen-reader announcements for pick-up, move, drop or cancel (no live region). ARIA 1.1 deprecated aria-grabbed/aria-dropeffect, so APG-style practice relies on live-region announcements and descriptive instructions. This is outside knowledge.

The factory writes no roles or states: no aria-selected for the selection, no aria-describedby instructions, no tabindex/roving focus for rows or handles. Focus is not kept on the moved item after a reorder.
There is no touch or pointer-events fallback. HTML drag-and-drop on touch devices is limited (outside knowledge), and the factory adds no long-press or threshold logic.
There is no auto-scroll, no placeholder, no disabled-item handling, no axis lock and no named groups or compatibility rules between containers.

Drag styles lack forced-colors handling, a styled 'into' state, a .selected style, tokenized sizes and colours, and variant support. AGENTS.md section 21 asks for tokens via --set-*, palette-each and forced-colors discipline on interactive chrome.
No event can be cancelled, so there is no gate before a drop or reorder. AGENTS.md section 14 provides dispatch() for cancelable pre-transition gates.

facts.fact: The plugin boots every `[data-vn-drag]` host; its direct children are items. The `data-vn-drag` value is reserved for a later group-transfer unit; Drag 1 reads only presence and exchanges nothing between hosts, even with matching values.

The author writes `draggable="true"` on the item or a grip handle; the module never adds or removes it. A grab is refused when there is no `[draggable="true"]` ancestor, when the handle is outside the item, when the item itself is draggable but also contains a draggable handle, or when it starts from an `input, textarea, select, button, a[href], [contenteditable]` descendant that is neither the item nor the handle.

The guide recommends a `div` host with `role="list"` and `role="listitem"` children, because the controller appends its `output` inside the host. Keyboard needs `tabindex="0"` on the item or a focusable handle such as a button.

The module writes `data-vn-dragging` on the source item at pointer dragstart and removes it in finish; it writes `data-vn-insert="before"|"after"` on one target item, rewriting only when target or side changes. It paints neither.

The plugin routes `pointerdown`, `dragstart`, `dragenter`, `dragover`, `dragleave`, `drop`, `dragend`, and `keydown` through selector `[data-vn-drag] > *`, with the trigger's parent as host. A clear path on `drop`, `dragend`, and Escape `keydown` calls `end()` on every `[data-vn-drag]` component in the target's document. The controller holds no listeners itself.

The pointer path is the native HTML Drag and Drop API only. `pointerdown` records the pressed target (no pointer capture, no movement threshold); `dragstart` emits `start`, sets `effectAllowed` and `dropEffect` to `move`, writes no payload, and calls `setDragImage(item, grab offset)`.

`dragenter`/`dragover`/`drop` are accepted (preventDefault) only while `this.#item` is a child of this host, so external text/files and cross-host items are not accepted. Events are handled only when they hit an item (a direct child); the owned output is skipped.

Insertion side is the pointer against the target's midpoint on the list axis. The axis comes from computed `display` flex/inline-flex, `flex-direction`, `writing-mode`, and `direction`; reversal flips the side. `#axis()` runs `getComputedStyle` on every `dragover` through `#side`.

`dragleave` clears the indicator only when `relatedTarget` is outside the host. Dragging over the source item clears the indicator. There is no placeholder element, no auto-scroll code, and no animation; the indicator is the attribute alone.
A drop computes `to` as the target's index among children without the source, plus 1 for `after`, then calls `#relocate(..., 'pointer')`. Dropping on the source item returns false.

`#relocate` emits cancelable `move`; it aborts if prevented, destroyed, or the session changed, and also returns false if a listener re-rendered the children synchronously. It moves with `moveBefore` when present, otherwise `insertBefore` plus focus restoration with `preventScroll`. The reference node is the owned output when the item goes last.

Escape calls `end()` unconditionally. A move needs Alt with no Ctrl, Meta, or Shift, not composing, and no outstanding session. The target must be the item or a `draggable="true"` element, and the item must be draggable or hold a draggable handle. ArrowUp/ArrowDown (vertical) or ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (horizontal) move one place with reversal applied. Movement stops at the ends with no wrap. Each key press emits `start`, then `move` (by `keyboard`), then `end`.
There is no grab or pick-up mode and no Home/End or Page keys. Each Alt+Arrow press is an atomic one-step move.

The constructor appends one `output` with `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic="true"`, and `aria-label="Sort status"` inside the host. The only text written is `Moved to position ${to + 1} of ${children.length}`, after a completed move. There is no announcement on grab, cancel, or refusal, and the item's name is not included. The module writes no other ARIA attribute.

The wire events are `start.vn.drag` `{item}` (cancelable; prevention refuses the grab), `move.vn.drag` `{item, from, to, by: 'pointer'|'keyboard'}` (cancelable; zero-based, with `to` counted after the item leaves its slot), and `end.vn.drag` `{item, moved}`. All are dispatched through the root `emitEvent`. `end` fires only when a session was admitted and the controller is not destroyed.

The exports are `Drag`, `DRAG_EVENTS`, `DRAG_DEFAULTS`, `createDrag`, and `createDragPlugin`, plus the types `DragInterface` (`receive`, `end`), `DragEventMap`, and `DragOptions` (`on` hooks only). `createDrag` settles one configured lifetime per host through a Registry. There are no options for axis, handle selector, group, disabled state, or drag image.

`destroy()` aborts the lifetime, calls `end()` (which clears the indicator and `data-vn-dragging`), removes the owned output, unbinds hooks, and releases registry ownership. It never touches `draggable`.

facts.fact: Planned shape: hosts with matching `data-vn-drag` values exchange items, and an empty value accepts only its own items. Alt+ArrowLeft/Right move to the previous or next host of the group. `move` gains `detail.source` and both hosts receive `end`. Styles are 'the Drag 1 fence's indicator plus one rule for an empty target host'. The specimen is a two-column Native specimen.

The elements prior art that was named: `createDrag.ts`, `createDrop.ts`, `_drag.scss`, `UseDragDropPage.vue`, `BoardExample.vue`. The addendum names a touch fallback (taking the `createPointer` shape: capture on press, `pointercancel` as end, `touch-action: none` on the handle only) and taking the target tint and insertion line from `_drag.scss:76-102` with Bootstrap color tokens. It holds back multi-selection, multi-item drag (`createDrag.ts:211-232`), and nesting (`into`).

The guide says 'A drop outside, Escape, or a refused move ends without a DOM move'. The departure row in the same guide says injected Escape during a native drag reaches no listener and does not cancel, and physical Escape is unestablished.

The brief and lane report say the plugin records the dragged item and its host. In code, the `Drag` controller instance holds `#item` and admits by `#item.parentElement === host`, and the plugin holds no session state.
The addendum's Drag 2 plan builds on 'the Drag 1 fence's indicator', but no fence shipped.

The guide says the output is excluded from item indexes. `#children()` excludes only the controller's own output, so an author-written `output` child (present in the factory test fixture) would count as an item. Inference from code: no test reads indexes with an authored output present.

gaps.gap: Missing: a pointer-events path (pointer capture, movement threshold, `pointercancel`). Only native HTML Drag and Drop is used, so touch on Android is unestablished and no touch fallback exists.
Missing: auto-scroll of the scroll container or viewport near edges while dragging. The controller has no scroll code.
Missing: a placeholder or gap preview, and any animated reflow. The indicator is a single attribute on the target.

Missing: a shipped style layer. There is no grab cursor, no `touch-action` on the handle, no reduced-motion transitions, no focus or grabbed visuals, and no Sass partial, so each consumer must paint state attributes itself (the showcase uses a MutationObserver adapter).
Missing keyboard features: a grab or pick-up mode (pick up, move, drop, cancel with restore), Home/End jumps, and announcements on grab, cancel, or refusal. Each Alt+Arrow press is atomic.
Live text lacks the item's name and gives no usage instructions (no `aria-describedby` hint). Only 'Moved to position N of M' is written.
Missing: cross-list transfer (Drag 2). The `data-vn-drag` value is ignored and matching groups exchange nothing.
Drops are accepted only on item children. An empty host, or host padding and gaps between items, can't receive a drop.
Axis detection is one-dimensional (flex row versus block). Inference: there is no midpoint handling for wrapped flex or CSS grid layouts.
Missing: multi-selection and multi-item drag, and nested lists (`into`).
Item identity is DOM index only, with no key in event details. There is also no `source` or target-element field in `move` detail.
Missing: options beyond hooks (axis override, handle selector, disabled or locked items, custom drag image). `DragOptions` carries only `on`.
Physical Escape cancellation of a native drag is unproven.
Inference, a performance concern: `getComputedStyle` is read on every `dragover`, with no throttle or cache.
Untested branches: the `insertBefore` fallback, reversed and rtl axes, the synchronous re-render path, destroy mid-drag, and refusals beyond `input`.

facts.topic: Hard boundary: cross-face Sass loads are refused
facts.fact: A conformance gate refuses every relative Sass load between the src/styles and src/bootstrap faces. `scanStyleLoads(readStyleSources())` must equal []. The forbidden forms are @use, @forward, @import, and meta.load-css(), in both directions. The planted controls include `src/styles/_tokens.scss @use '../bootstrap/tokens'` and `@forward '../bootstrap/mixins'`. So a styles-layer partial cannot use `@use '../bootstrap/...'` today.

`scanStyleLoads` checks only targets that match `^\.\.?\/` (line 429), and it classifies faces only under src/bootstrap and src/styles (lines 393-396). A bare `@use 'bootstrap'` is not flagged (setup.test.ts:61, 71-114), and neither is a `pkg:` URL. INFERENCE: a package-specifier load such as `pkg:@orkestrel/veneer/bootstrap/scss` would pass this scanner. That is a loophole, not a sanctioned path; no rule or guide line permits it.

AGENTS.md (scaffold) says no extension face imports another extension's face. Its one exception is a styles extension that builds another extension's recreation for a utility library (src/tailwindcss building Bootstrap), which may @use that extension's Sass partials configured through their _tokens.scss switches. src/styles is the base styles surface, not that tailwindcss exception.

facts.topic: Published Bootstrap Sass entry and its namespace
facts.fact: package.json exports `./bootstrap/scss` -> `./src/bootstrap/index.scss` and `./styles/scss` -> `./src/styles/index.scss`. src/bootstrap/index.scss forwards only `$layered` (`@forward 'tokens' show $layered;`) and then @uses reset, elements, components, and utilities. A consumer of the barrel therefore sees only the `$layered` member: no maps, no mixins, no functions. INFERENCE (Sass default): the namespace is the last URL segment, for example `scss` for `.../bootstrap/scss` or `index` for `../bootstrap/index`.

The only configurable variable is `$layered: true !default`. It is declared in _tokens.scss and forwarded to mixins through `@use 'mixins' with ($layered: $layered)`. Fixtures configure it with `@use '.../bootstrap/tokens' with ($layered: false)`, and the guide shows `@use 'pkg:@orkestrel/veneer/bootstrap/scss' with ($layered: false)`. No map (`$utilities`, `$breakpoints`) carries `!default`, so none can be configured.

_tokens.scss emits the layer order statement when `$layered` is true (lines 8-10) and a license comment (12-16). Under `@include mixins.layer` it also emits every `--bs-*` custom property for `:root,[data-bs-theme='light']` (19-138) and for `[data-bs-theme='dark']` (139-193). These cover theme colors and their -rgb, -text-emphasis, -bg-subtle, and -border-subtle forms (44-83), radii (120-126), shadows (127-130), and focus ring (131-133). All are CSS custom properties written as string interpolations. There is no Sass map of theme colors.

The members are `$layered` (6) and three mixins. `reboot` wraps `layer` (8-12). `layer` writes `@layer bootstrap { @content }`, or bare content when `$layered` is false (14-22). `utility($utility, $infix: '')` emits `.{class}{infix}-{key}` rules from one utility map entry; it honors class, property, values, state, css-var, css-variable-name, and local-vars, and it routes every declaration through `unlayer` as !important (24-76). `unlayer($declarations)` emits !important declarations at-root without layer (79-100). The partial has no @function, uses sass:list, map, and string, and emits no top-level CSS.

`$utilities` (6-1033) holds Bootstrap 5.3.8 utility keys. The per-theme-color value lists are 'focus-ring' (106-120), 'border-color' (211-229), 'subtle-border-color' (230-243), 'color' (763-789), 'text-color' emphasis (800-813), 'link-underline' (836-853), 'background-color' (867-889), and 'subtle-background-color' (901-914). The spacer scale 0/1/2/3/4/5 = 0/.25rem/.5rem/1rem/1.5rem/3rem appears only inside margin* (437-534), padding* (535-625), and gap/row-gap/column-gap (626-664). Font sizes are 'font-size' with values and an rfs map (672-689). Radii are 'rounded*' (939-1013). Shadows are 'shadow' (96-105). `$breakpoints` is (sm 576px, md 768px, lg 992px, xl 1200px, xxl 1400px) (1035-1041). There is no standalone $theme-colors, $spacers, $grid-breakpoints, or $font-sizes map.

facts.topic: Component-scoped custom properties in Bootstrap partials
facts.fact: Bootstrap component partials declare component-scoped tokens as string interpolations on the selector, for example `.btn { --bs-btn-padding-x: #{'0.75rem'}; ... --bs-btn-focus-box-shadow: ... }`. Rules then read them through var().

The shared order is `@layer reset, bootstrap, theme, elements, components, surfaces, composables, modifiers, utilities;`. It is declared in src/styles/_tokens.scss:2 unconditionally and in src/bootstrap/_tokens.scss:9 under `@if $layered`. The fixture tests/fixtures/styles/bootstrap.scss:1 opens with it. LAYER_ORDER and LAYER_STATEMENT are defined in tests/setup.ts:1156-1169.

facts.topic: Which layer a veneer component lands in
facts.fact: The rule says: 'Put ... a class skin that applies with no script running in components/', and 'Each partial uses its folder's own layer' and must never wrap rules in a foreign layer. A src/styles/components partial therefore writes `@layer components`. The styles proof requires every layer block and every declaration placement to be in the owned list (theme, reset, elements, components, surfaces, composables, modifiers, utilities). Unlayered declarations (layer undefined) and the `bootstrap` layer both fail that proof. INFERENCE: Bootstrap's `layer` mixin (writes @layer bootstrap) and `unlayer` (writes outside every layer) would each break tests/src/styles/index.test.ts if used in src/styles.

SHEET_LAYERS gives the owned layers per built sheet: bootstrap = ['bootstrap']; styles = [theme, reset, elements, components, surfaces, composables, modifiers, utilities]; themes = ['theme']. A proof requires each pair of built sheets to share no class name in any shared layer.

A styles-sheet rule may declare a Bootstrap class name to record an addition, and it wins over Bootstrap by layer order. A `surfaces` rule beats a `bootstrap` rule on the same class in all 6 load permutations (fixture .probe: margin-top 3px, padding-top 5px). An unlayered consumer rule beats every rule the styles sheet writes. surfaces, composables, and modifiers precede utilities.

results.subject: What the primary sources say about building a veneer sortable list: reordering Bootstrap list items by pointer and keyboard, with cross-list transfer as a later unit. Covers HTML DnD, Pointer Events, DOM moveBefore, ARIA/APG reordering, WCAG 2.5.7, prefers-reduced-motion, and Chromium 141/153 status. All web sources fetched 2026-10-08.

facts.fact: The local W3C corpus has almost no sortable or reorder material. Searching for sortable, reorder, aria-grabbed, dropeffect, moveBefore, setPointerCapture, pointercancel and rearrangeable found only 2 hits, both in texts.md: a table-sorting example (`<script src="sortable.js">`, `<table class="sortable">`). That example is about sorting by column value, not drag reordering.

The only drag-and-drop entry in the corpus is a summary of the draggable attribute: "an enumerated attribute with states `true` and `false`". Some elements (`img`, `a[href]`, selections) are draggable by default.
aria.md has no entries for live regions, aria-grabbed, aria-dropeffect or reordering. It only maps implicit roles, e.g. `output` → `status` and `select[multiple]` → `listbox`.

HTML DnD is framed around a pointing device and mousedown: "On a visual medium with a pointing device, a drag operation could be the default action of a `mousedown` event". It sets no user-agent requirement for touch or keyboard. The introduction only says users "would probably have to explicitly indicate their intention" (non-normative).

The HTML DnD section has no keyboard-access requirement. Its only accessibility text says draggable elements "should also have a title attribute that names the element for the purpose of non-visual interactions."

During dragenter and dragover the drag data store is in protected mode, where "the data itself is unavailable". In that mode getData returns the empty string. A drop target therefore cannot read the payload until the drop event.

facts.topic: HTML DnD: drop effects and cancellation
facts.fact: dropEffect accepts "none", "copy", "link", and "move". effectAllowed "Can be set (during the dragstart event)". dragover "also needs to be canceled" for a drop to be accepted. dragend is not cancelable and fires at the source node.

facts.topic: HTML DnD: pointer stream ends at dragstart
facts.fact: In the processing model, step 10 runs after dragstart: "Fire a pointer event at the source node named pointercancel". Once a native drag starts, the source's pointer event stream ends, so native DnD cannot be combined with a pointer-capture drag on the same gesture.

facts.topic: Chromium: pointer suppression on drag start
facts.fact: Chromestatus entry 6732314958757888, "Pointer event suppression on drag start", is "Proposed" with desktop milestone 148 and no Android milestone. Its motivation: "the user agent must notify the drag source that it will no longer receive pointer events". The search summary says Android already partly behaves this way for touch drags.
Pointer Events Level 3 is a W3C Recommendation dated 30 June 2026 and supersedes Level 2.

setPointerCapture only works while the pointer is in its active buttons state; "otherwise it fails silently". It throws NotFoundError when the pointerId does not match an active pointer, and InvalidStateError when the element is not connected.

"Immediately after firing the pointerup or pointercancel events, the user agent MUST clear the pending pointer capture target override". If the capture target is "no longer connected", the override "SHOULD be set to the document" and lostpointercapture fires at the document.
gotpointercapture fires "when an element receives pointer capture". lostpointercapture "MUST be fired prior to any subsequent events for the pointer after capture was released".

facts.topic: Pointer Events: implicit capture on touch
facts.fact: On pointerdown, if "the associated device is a direct manipulation device, and the target is an Element, then set pointer capture" happens implicitly. hasPointerCapture "may be used (for instance, in a pointerdown listener)" to detect this.

The UA fires pointercancel "when it detects a scenario to suppress a pointer event stream". One listed scenario is the pointer being "used by the user agent to manipulate the page viewport (e.g. panning or zooming)".

Panning and zooming cannot be canceled through pointer events: "Authors must instead use touch-action". With touch-action none, interactions "MUST NOT trigger behaviors related to viewport panning and zooming". Later changes to touch-action "will be ignored for the duration of the action". Spec examples use `touch-action: none` so pointer events reach the application.
touch-action "applies to all forms of pointer inputs that allow direct manipulation for panning and zooming". A desktop mouse, which pans with scrollbars, is not direct manipulation.

The DOM spec's summary note reads: "Moves, without first removing, movedNode into node after child if child is non-null; otherwise after the last child of node." However, the method steps set referenceChild and "move node into this before referenceChild" (a likely editorial inconsistency; see gaps). The note also says "This method preserves state associated with movedNode".

The move algorithm throws HierarchyRequestError when the shadow-including roots differ, when node is a host-including inclusive ancestor of newParent, or when node is not an Element or CharacterData node, among other cases. It also throws when "the state associated with the moved node cannot be preserved." NotFoundError is thrown when child's parent is not newParent.
A move runs "the live range pre-remove steps" and queues two tree mutation records: one removal for oldParent, then one insertion for newParent. MutationObservers therefore see a remove and an add.
For custom descendants, a move enqueues the "connectedMoveCallback" reaction. MDN says it "is run instead of connectedCallback() and disconnectedCallback()".

MDN lists the state moveBefore preserves: animation and transition state, iframe loading state, "Interactivity states (for example, :focus and :active)", fullscreen element state, popover open state, and modal dialog state.

MDN: moveBefore "can only work when moving a node within the same document". It also "won't work" when moving between disconnected and connected trees. As a fallback, MDN advises: "use Node.insertBefore() instead, or use try...catch".
Chromestatus "DOM State-Preserving Move" (5135990159835136) is "Enabled by default", shipped in milestone 133 on desktop and Android. The Chrome blog says it is "available in Chrome version 133".

Browser compat data for api.Element.moveBefore: Chrome 133 (Chrome Android and Edge follow Chrome), Firefox 144, Safari `version_added: false` with impl_url https://webkit.org/b/281223 (iOS Safari follows Safari). MDN calls it "not Baseline".

Version support: setPointerCapture Chrome 55, Firefox 59, Safari 13. touch-action Chrome 36, Safari 13, iOS Safari 9.3. DragEvent Chrome 46, Safari 14, with Chrome Android and iOS Safari following desktop.

Chromium dashboard stable dates: M141 stable_date 2025-09-30; M153 stable_date 2026-09-08 (early stable 2026-08-26). Both are above 133, so moveBefore, setPointerCapture and touch-action are all shipped in both.

Both attributes are marked "[Deprecated in ARIA 1.1]". Each "is expected to be replaced by a new feature in a future version of WAI-ARIA", and "Authors are therefore advised to treat aria-grabbed as deprecated" (same wording for aria-dropeffect).
For deprecated features, "it is recommended that authors do not use it for new content".
"Elements with the role status have an implicit aria-live value of polite." The alert role "will be processed as an atomic live region" with assertive politeness.

In the rearrangeable listbox example, the Up and Down move commands are Alt + Up Arrow and Alt + Down Arrow. Focus stays on the listbox and aria-activedescendant identifies the focused option. "Live regions provide confirmation of completed actions." The shortcut keeps focus on the moved option so screen reader users can "hear the position of an option after it is moved." Moves are also exposed through toolbar buttons.

The listbox role "does not support interacting with elements inside of an option" (links, buttons, checkboxes). The APG points to the Grid Pattern for those. Horizontal lists need aria-orientation="horizontal". Home and End support is "strongly recommended for lists with more than five options."

"All functionality that uses a dragging movement for operation can be achieved by a single pointer without dragging", unless dragging is essential or user-agent determined. Keyboard support alone does not satisfy it: "achieving keyboard equivalence for a dragging operation does not automatically meet this success criterion." Example: "A sortable list of elements may, after tapping or clicking on a list element, provide adjacent controls."

prefers-reduced-motion is "used to detect if the user has requested the system minimize the amount of non-essential motion it uses." The `reduce` value means the user prefers an interface that "removes or replaces the types of motion-based animation"; `no-preference` is false in a boolean context. Media Queries 5 is a Working Draft dated 29 June 2026.

The elements repo's createPointer factory already uses setPointerCapture, hasPointerCapture/releasePointerCapture, and a pointercancel end handler. This is a lead for the drag engine; no sortable factory exists there.

facts.topic: Matrix: native HTML DnD as the drag engine
facts.fact: For: shipped widely (DragEvent Chrome 46, Safari 14) and offers dropEffect move/copy for cross-list transfer. Against: no keyboard requirement, touch behavior not specified, payload unreadable in protected mode during dragover, and pointercancel fires at the source on dragstart.

facts.topic: Matrix: Pointer Events plus capture as the drag engine
facts.fact: For: a Recommendation (2026-06-30) supported in Chrome 55, Firefox 59 and Safari 13; touch-action:none stops pan/zoom from cancelling the drag; capture keeps events on the source. Against: capture is lost silently if not in the active buttons state, it moves to the document if the target is disconnected, and touch-action changes mid-gesture are ignored.

For: preserves focus, :active, animations and popover/dialog state; Chrome 133+ and Firefox 144. Against: Safari has not shipped it (version_added false); throws on cross-document or connected/disconnected moves; MutationObservers still see remove plus add records. MDN advises an insertBefore fallback.
Against: deprecated in ARIA 1.1, and authors are advised not to use them in new content. For: none found in primary sources.

facts.topic: Matrix: keyboard reorder via Alt+Arrow with live-region confirmation
facts.fact: For: the APG rearrangeable listbox uses Alt+Up/Down with a live region confirming completed actions, and keeps focus on the moved option. Against: the listbox role disallows interactive content inside options (APG points to Grid). Under WCAG 2.5.7, keyboard support alone does not meet the single-pointer requirement.
facts.citation: APG listbox-rearrangeable; APG listbox pattern; WCAG 2.5.7 Understanding

gaps.gap: Unresolved: the DOM spec's moveBefore summary says "after child" but the method steps insert "before referenceChild". The fetched text did not settle whether this is editorial. Tests should establish the observed behavior (before child).

Unknown whether active pointer capture survives when the captured element is moved with moveBefore, or with insertBefore (remove then re-insert). §9.5 covers only a target that is "no longer connected", and neither MDN nor the Chrome blog lists pointer capture among preserved state.
The DOM spec defines no specific state list for moveBefore. MDN and the Chrome blog give examples only. Whether text selection and :hover survive was not stated.

Safari has no moveBefore (BCD version_added false, webkit.org/b/281223). A production sortable needs a feature-detected insertBefore fallback, plus explicit focus restoration and animation handling on that path.

No primary source defines a successor to aria-grabbed and aria-dropeffect. The ARIA editor's draft fetch (2 Oct 2026) was truncated before the property definitions, so their status in ARIA 1.3 (still deprecated or removed) is unknown.

No primary source fetched gives a normative announcement-text pattern for a sortable (e.g. grab, move "position N of M", drop, cancel messages). The APG example says only that live regions confirm completed actions. Its exact markup (aria-live value, role) was not quoted.

Choosing between the listbox role (plain options only) and grid or list semantics for Bootstrap list-group items that contain buttons or links is not settled by the APG beyond pointing to the Grid Pattern for interactive content.
WCAG 2.5.7 needs a single-pointer, non-drag alternative (e.g. tap to select, then move controls). A pointer-drag plus keyboard sortable without one would not meet AA.

Native HTML DnD touch behavior on Chrome Android and iOS Safari is not specified by HTML. BCD shows only that DragEvent mirrors desktop versions; the actual touch drag initiation behavior was not established.

Chromium's pointer-suppression-on-dragstart change (5135990159835136's sibling 6732314958757888) is "Proposed" at M148. Whether it shipped by M153 is not shown, so pointercancel timing on native dragstart may differ between Chromium 141 and 153.
The exact Pointer Events §8.2 sentence on when touch-action is sampled (at touch start) was not captured verbatim. Only "ignored for the duration of the action" was quoted.

No primary source fetched covers auto-scrolling the scroll container during a pointer drag, hit-testing or placeholder geometry, or Escape-to-cancel semantics. These are production behaviors that need a design decision rather than a spec citation.

No primary source settles whether a sortable should animate reorder with FLIP transitions or View Transitions under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. MQ5 says only that reduce removes or replaces non-essential motion.

Is the drag engine Pointer Events with capture and touch-action:none (recommended by the evidence for touch), with native HTML DnD reserved, or not used, for the later cross-list unit?

corrected.claim: Input model: createDrag listens for dragstart, dragend, dragenter, dragover, dragleave and drop on the host.
corrected.correction: These listeners are conditional. dragstart and dragend are added only when isSource is true. dragenter, dragover, dragleave and drop are added only when isTarget is true. With the defaults (auto:true, no list, no items, no effect.drop), isTarget is false. Such a host is a drag source only: it never calls preventDefault on dragover, never emits over or drop, and never reorders. Only click and mousedown on the host, plus the three document listeners, are always added.

corrected.claim: State sync: syncRows rewrites every row's classes and draggable flag. queueSync runs it again in a microtask so rows that Vue re-renders get fixed up.
corrected.correction: syncRows always rewrites the classes, but it writes draggable only when isSource && auto. contract: Role: repair writer. No public type changes. Depends on the precondition finding: the app browser project is green at the base commit, or its 2 failures are recorded as unrelated with their run.

Wrap every relocation so `#finish` runs on every exit path. When `moveBefore` throws a `DOMException`, fall back once to `insertBefore` with focus restored using `preventScroll`. On any other throw, finish with `moved:false` and rethrow.
Consult `#pressed` only when `item.contains(this.#pressed)`. Otherwise use the dragstart target.
Fix the row-axis reversal: `reversed` for a flex row is `(direction === 'rtl') !== (writingMode === 'sideways-lr')`, still XOR the flex `*-reverse` flag. The column branch is unchanged.

units.title: Hit-test slots on the host and write the physical edge
contract: Role: feature writer. Depends on drag-2.

Types first: declare in types.ts the pure slot contract that helpers.ts exports, with readonly inputs: the item boxes in order, the point, the axis `{ horizontal, reversed }`, and the source index. The result is the insertion index among the items without the source, plus the physical edge `'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'`, or `undefined` when the slot is the source's own position.

helpers.ts exports one pure `{verb}{Noun}` function for that contract (proposed `findSlot`). It resolves the slot by comparing the point against item midpoints along the axis, so padding, `gap` space, and the end of the list all resolve. It reads no DOM. index.ts exports it through the module barrel.

plugins.ts routes `dragenter`, `dragover`, `dragleave`, and `drop` on the host itself as well as on `[data-vn-drag] > *`. The host resolves to itself. `pointerdown`, `dragstart`, `dragend`, and `keydown` stay item-only.

Drag.ts accepts dragover and drop anywhere inside the host while its own item is in flight. It computes the slot through the helper and relocates to the slot index. It writes `data-vn-insert` with the physical edge on the item adjacent to the slot: the leading edge of the item after the slot, or the trailing edge of the last item for an end slot. It rewrites the attribute only when the item or the edge changes. It writes no indicator for the source's own slot.
The host carries `data-vn-over` while an admitted drag is over it. The attribute is removed on a `dragleave` whose `relatedTarget` is outside the host, and in `#finish`.
An item whose `aria-disabled` is `true` refuses grabs by pointer and keyboard and stays a slot neighbor. The module reads ARIA only, never a Bootstrap class.
Read the axis per event as in Drag 1. Add no cache, because no measurement of the cost exists.
Guide: the § Sortable list data-attribute table documents `data-vn-insert` values as physical edges and adds `data-vn-over`.
Tension for the subjective lane: physical edge values versus the logical `before` and `after` they replace, and the names `findSlot` and `data-vn-over`.
proofs: tests/src/browser/drags/helpers.test.ts (Node or Chromium, pure): the end slot, the start slot, gap space, the source's own slot returning undefined, and reversed and horizontal axes, each with expected index and edge.

units.title: Paint the sortable in the styles layer
contract: Role: styles writer. Depends on drag-3, and on the user's answer to the question that opens the styles chunk and the showcase sheet. Loads nothing from src/bootstrap: every Bootstrap value arrives as a `var(--bs-*)` reference, so this unit needs no map and no gate change.

_mixins.scss gains `transition($value...)`, which emits `transition` and, inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, `transition: none`. It also gains `reduced-motion`, which wraps `@content` in that media query. Both emit no top-level CSS.

surfaces/_drag.scss writes `@layer surfaces` once. On a handle inside a host item (`[data-vn-drag] > [draggable='true']` and `[data-vn-drag] > * [draggable='true']`), it sets `cursor: grab`, `touch-action: none`, and `user-select: none`. Inside an `[aria-disabled='true']` item, the cursor reverts to `default`.

composables/_drag.scss writes `@layer composables` once. It declares component-scoped `--vn-drag-size: calc(var(--bs-border-width) * 2)` and `--vn-drag-opacity` on `[data-vn-drag]`. The source `[data-vn-drag] > [data-vn-dragging]` takes `opacity: var(--vn-drag-opacity)` through the `transition` mixin.

Indicator: `[data-vn-drag] > [data-vn-insert]` takes `position: relative`. Its `::after` (never `::before`, which `.list-group-numbered` owns) is absolutely positioned with `pointer-events: none`, sits above `.list-group-item.active`'s `z-index: 2`, and draws the line as a border of width `--vn-drag-size` on the named edge. One `@each` over the four physical edges generates the edge rules from one partial-local map (edge to cross-axis insets). The insets are physical.

Indicator color resolves on the item: `var(--vn-drag-color, var(--bs-list-group-active-bg, var(--bs-primary)))`. Bootstrap's contextual `list-group-item-{color}` variants then retint the line through the tokens they already set, with no per-color rule. On `.active`, the line uses `--bs-list-group-active-color`.
Over state: `[data-vn-drag][data-vn-over]` takes a `color-mix(in oklab, …, transparent)` tint of the same color. An empty host (`:not(:has(> *))`) adds a dashed outline of `--vn-drag-size`.
Under `@media (forced-colors: active)`, the line and the outline use `Highlight`. Nothing uses box-shadow. The partial writes no literal color.

Showcase, in the same change if the user rules yes: app/browser loads the built ./styles sheet beside ./bootstrap, deletes the MutationObserver adapter (Showcase.ts:135-152), and the journey reads geometry, not classes. Guide § Sortable list replaces 'no stylesheet' with the partials' contract.

Tension: whether the sortable needs a theme-color modifier (`.drag-{color}` generated from the theme-color map). This design omits it. No consumer exists, and the contextual tokens already vary the line. If the subjective lane adds it, it waits on the map ruling.
proofs: tests/src/styles/surfaces/drag.test.ts and tests/src/styles/composables/drag.test.ts under Chromium 141 and 153, with the built ./bootstrap and ./styles sheets adopted. The variation matrix is generated from `CLASS_NAMES.bootstrap`: plain, flush, and numbered list groups, `list-group-horizontal`, each `list-group-horizontal-{bp}` at widths on both sides of its `$breakpoints` boundary, each contextual `list-group-item-{color}`, `.active`, and `.disabled`, in light and dark `data-bs-theme`.

Per matrix cell, with `data-vn-insert` set to each edge directly (the attribute is the contract): the `::after` border width on the named edge equals `--vn-drag-size` and is 0 on the others; its color equals the item's resolved active background, or the active color on `.active`; the item's `getBoundingClientRect` is unchanged with the attribute on; the numbered `::before` content is unchanged; and the last item keeps Bootstrap's bottom radii.

Under emulated `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the source's computed `transition-duration` is `0s`. Under emulated `forced-colors: active`, the line keeps a non-zero border width. On the handle, the computed `cursor` is `grab` and `touch-action` is `none`. Every block of each partial sits in its folder's layer, read through `readPlacement`. An author `opacity-25` on an item still wins, which pins the documented direction.

Controls: moving the composables rule into `@layer bootstrap` reddens placement; drawing the line with box-shadow reddens the forced-colors case; drawing it with `border-top` on the item reddens the geometry case; `::before` reddens the numbered case.

units.styles: Two partials, because the folder law splits one component by job. surfaces/_drag.scss holds the attribute API the markup carries before any script runs: grab cursor, touch-action, and user-select on the handle. composables/_drag.scss holds the chrome the engine's state attributes drive: dim, edge line, and over tint. contract: Role: feature writer. Depends on drag-2 and drag-3 (the disabled refusal).

units.title: Transfer between hosts of one group
contract: Role: feature writer. Depends on drag-3 (host-level slots and `data-vn-over`), drag-4 (empty-host paint), and drag-5 (commands).
Types first: `move` detail gains `source: HTMLElement`, the host the item leaves, which equals the event's host for an in-list move. `from` indexes the source and `to` indexes the target.
Hosts whose `data-vn-drag` values are equal and non-empty form a group. An empty value accepts only its own items, as in Drag 1.

No shared session and no payload: the target controller derives the dragged item from the document's `[data-vn-dragging]` element whose parent host shares its non-empty group value. `dataTransfer` still carries no data. External drags stay refused.
`move` is dispatched, cancelable, on the target host. `start` and `end` stay on the source host. The target writes its own live text.

Keyboard: Alt+Arrow along the axis perpendicular to the host's list axis moves the item to the previous or next group host in document order, at the same index clamped to the target's length. Focus stays on the handle. Ends of the group emit nothing. This resolves the addendum's collision with the row-axis keys.
Commands: two host-to-host commands for the same moves (names for the subjective lane; proposed `--backward` and `--forward`), routed like drag-5.
Specimen and guide: a two-column Native board specimen; § Sortable list documents groups, `source`, and the perpendicular keys.

Tension: the addendum has both hosts receive `end`; this design keeps `end` on the session owner and gives the target `move` only. Tension: whether the target's live text names the target list from its `aria-label`.
proofs: tests/src/browser/drags/plugins.test.ts under Chromium 141 and 153 with real CDP drags across two group hosts: order in both hosts, the detail with `source`, `start` and `end` on the source, `move` on the target, prevention leaving both hosts unchanged, a drop on an empty group host, hosts with different values or an empty value refusing, external text and files refused, no `text/plain` payload, and the perpendicular Alt+Arrow and both commands.
Controls: deriving the item without the group check reddens the different-value case; dispatching `move` on the source reddens the target-listener case.
units.styles: composables/_drag.scss gains nothing beyond drag-4's empty-host outline unless the board specimen shows a gap. Any rule added stays in `@layer composables` and reads the same tokens.

units.title: Drag by touch and pen through pointer events
contract: Role: feature writer. Depends on drag-3 (the pure slot helper) and drag-4 (`touch-action: none` on the handle). Mouse keeps native drag and drop.

For a `pointerdown` whose `pointerType` is `touch` or `pen` on an admitted handle (same refusals as dragstart, including `aria-disabled`), the controller arms a session. It captures the pointer on the host, not on the item, so a move cannot drop the capture.

The session starts when movement exceeds a slop named in constants.ts. The slop must keep a tap on a grip button a click. At start, the controller emits start (cancelable) and writes `data-vn-dragging`.

Each `pointermove` hit-tests through the slot helper and writes `data-vn-insert` and `data-vn-over` as the native path does. `pointerup` relocates with `by: 'pointer'`. `pointercancel`, `lostpointercapture` before `pointerup`, Escape, and destroy end with `moved:false` and release the capture.
A `dragstart` that arrives while a touch session is armed is prevented, so one gesture never runs both engines.

Auto-scroll: while the pointer sits within an edge zone of the nearest scrollable ancestor or the viewport, each `pointermove` scrolls that container by a step proportional to the depth into the zone. No timer or animation-frame loop runs; this follows the no-polling law.

Guide: § Sortable list states that the touch path needs `touch-action: none` on the handle from ./styles or from the author, and records Android behavior as unestablished unless the user rules a device proof.
Tension: scrolling advances only while the finger moves, which an animation-frame loop would avoid but the no-polling law forbids. Tension: the source stays in place with no floating preview.
proofs: tests/src/browser/drags/Drag.test.ts under Chromium 141 and 153 with a touch-enabled context and CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent`: reorder by touch with start, move, and end; a tap under the slop still clicks the grip and moves nothing; touchCancel ends with `moved:false`; destroy mid-gesture releases the capture and removes the attributes; `window.scrollY` stays unchanged during a drag on the handle; an edge-zone drag scrolls a scrollable host; mouse still takes the native path.
Controls: capturing on the item and then moving it reddens the capture case; omitting the dragstart suppression reddens the one-engine case.
units.styles: Uses drag-4's surfaces rule (`touch-action: none` and `user-select: none` on the handle). Adds no rule.
